audit_findings.title: Nonrecurring tariff refunds materially inflate the FY2026 owner-earnings anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: approximately $9.184 million pretax (2.0% of $459.178 million sales) or $6.943 million after tax using the filed 24.4% effective rate; 21.7% of the $32.0 million OE anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: The refund increases FY2026 earnings and cash flow embedded in anchor OE, which is capitalized through every forecast year and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: The 250-bps increase was primarily driven by a 200-bps benefit from the International Emergency Economic Powers Act ("IEEPA") Tariff Refunds received and to a lesser extent favorable mix driven by product and customer portfolio optimization initiatives.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that tariff refunds supplied 200 of the 250 basis points of FY2026 gross-margin improvement and that substantially all eligible refunds had been received. This is an exceptional benefit rather than recurring operating performance. If the computed after-tax benefit passed fully into OE, holding all other assumptions fixed would reduce indicated value by approximately $16.40, $21.64 and $25.49 per share in the bear, base and bull cases, respectively; the base value would fall from $103.34 to about $81.70, slightly below the $82.16 market price. The exact OE adjustment remains subject to cash-flow reconciliation, but materiality is demonstrated.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the refund through cost of goods sold, inventory, taxes and operating cash flow; remove the verified after-tax amount from FY2026 OE and rerun all scenarios and the buy-below price.

audit_findings.title: A scheduled tariff increase could reverse recent margin gains
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; filed scheduled rate increase is 5 percentage points, from 25% to 30%, on the majority of seating products sourced from Vietnam and manufactured in Mexico
audit_findings.mechanism: Unmitigated incremental tariffs would raise cost of goods sold and reduce prospective OE and sustainable growth margins.
audit_findings.evidence: The majority of our seating products sourced from Vietnam and manufactured in Mexico remain subject to the 25% Section 232 tariffs which, under the existing proclamation, is scheduled to increase to 30% effective January 1, 2027, unless modified prior to that date, and are generally not subject to the additional Section 301 tariffs.
audit_findings.explanation: The scheduled January 1, 2027 increase is forward-looking and expressly subject to modification. The filing establishes broad product exposure but provides neither the affected import value nor the net effect of pricing, supplier concessions, sourcing changes or inventory timing. It therefore cannot presently be converted into an OE adjustment, but it should be monitored because the valuation projects growth from FY2026 margins without an explicit tariff step-up.
audit_findings.action: At each reporting date, verify whether the 30% rate became effective and obtain affected import costs and realized mitigation; rerun OE and growth scenarios if a net cost is demonstrated.

audit_findings.title: Underfunded multi-employer pension exposure may represent an unrecognized senior claim
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified potential liability; filed FY2026 contribution was $0.111 million, 0.35% of the $32.0 million OE anchor, covering 6 employees
audit_findings.mechanism: Higher rehabilitation contributions would reduce future OE, while withdrawal liability or assessments would be a claim on equity value not included in the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Based on the most recent information available to the Company, the present value of actuarially accrued liabilities of the multi-employer pension plan substantially exceeds the value of the assets held in trust to pay benefits.
audit_findings.explanation: The red-zone status and substantial plan underfunding are demonstrated, but no Flexsteel withdrawal-liability estimate is filed. The known annual contribution is small relative to anchor OE, yet it does not bound exposure because multi-employer liability can include allocated underfunding and obligations associated with other employers. The record therefore cannot establish whether the senior claim is material.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the latest funding notice, rehabilitation schedule, employer-allocation data and a formal withdrawal-liability estimate; deduct any probable one-time claim from the bridge and incorporate recurring contribution increases into OE.

audit_findings.title: Tariff-refund claims could consume cash already capitalized as earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; the related FY2026 earnings benefit computes to approximately $9.184 million pretax, but the filing gives no asserted-claim or reserve amount
audit_findings.mechanism: A settlement could reduce operating cash or create a liability ahead of common equity; if treated as a recurring margin reversal, it could also reduce normalized OE.
audit_findings.evidence: Retail partners, suppliers, distributors or other parties may assert claims seeking reimbursement, credits or other payments relating to some or all of these tariff refunds.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that third parties may seek reimbursement, but it does not establish that claims have been asserted, that contracts require pass-through, or that a payment is probable. The $9.184 million computed P&L benefit indicates the relevant scale but is not a proven claim ceiling because the gross refunds and contractual entitlements are undisclosed. Materiality consequently remains unresolved. Any adjustment must avoid double-counting amounts already removed when normalizing the nonrecurring refund.
audit_findings.action: Review customer and supplier contracts, post-year-end claims, legal correspondence and reserve analysis; quantify probable payments, then reduce cash or OE as appropriate without duplicating the normalization in finding 1.

audit_findings.title: The purported dilution ceiling counts PSUs only at target performance
audit_findings.magnitude: 161,000 target-level unvested PSUs, equal to 3.6% of the 4.512237 million-share valuation denominator; incremental maximum shares are unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Above-target PSU vesting increases the fully diluted share denominator and reduces value per share without changing aggregate owner earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: The table below sets forth, as of June 30, 2026, the number of unvested PSUs granted at the target performance level for the 2024-2026, 2025-2027, and 2026-2028 performance periods under the 2022 Plan and the number of unvested RSUs granted in conjunction with the PSUs.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that the disclosed 161,000 PSUs are measured only at target, so that amount cannot by itself establish a maximum dilution ceiling. The maximum payout multiplier and performance attainment are absent from the supplied record. Target PSUs are already material enough to identify the scale, but the incremental dilution above target cannot be determined or tested against the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Read the governing PSU agreements and proxy disclosure for maximum payout multipliers and current performance attainment; replace target PSUs with maximum issuable or support a probability-weighted denominator, then rerun per-share values.

audit_findings.title: Adding all cash assumes none is required for operations
audit_findings.magnitude: maximum $16.678 million, or $3.70 per diluted share
audit_findings.mechanism: Any minimum operating-cash requirement reduces excess cash added in the equity bridge dollar for dollar.
audit_findings.evidence: Working capital (current assets less current liabilities) on June 30, 2026, was $82.7 million compared to $110.4 million on June 30, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: Even the conservative extreme of treating all $16.678 million as operating cash would reduce bear, base and bull values to approximately $75.47, $99.64 and $117.56 per share. The market price of $82.16 would remain above bear value and below base and bull values, while the buy-below price would decline from $72.34 to approximately $69.75 and remain below market. Thus the full possible adjustment does not change the valuation conclusion; an evidence-based partial adjustment would be smaller.
audit_findings.action: Document minimum operating cash using monthly liquidity, working-capital needs and revolver usage, and subtract the supported amount from bridge cash in the next rerun.
